name: Hartley information measure and transmission
description: A quantitative information measure based on distinguishable symbol sequences, used to compare communication systems.

impact.note: Gave communication engineers a first numerical measure of information for comparing systems; its main known successor is Shannon's theory, which supplied the generality.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: Hartley presented Transmission of Information at the International Congress of Telegraphy and Telephony.

evidence.supports: Hartley presents an information measure and identifies the September 1927 presentation.

events.caveats: The surviving paper says it was presented at the 1927 meeting and published in July 1928; this is not the later probability-weighted entropy theory.
